extra_misconceptions.fact: Doctors of Osteopathic Medicine hold full medical licenses to prescribe drugs and perform surgery across all specialties.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Osteopathic physicians only perform spinal adjustments and cannot prescribe medications or perform surgery.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Ophthalmologists complete medical school and surgical residency, while optometrists earn an OD degree for primary vision care.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Optometrists and ophthalmologists complete the exact same medical school residency to treat eye diseases.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Psychiatrists are medical doctors who prescribe medication, whereas psychologists focus on behavioral therapy and assessment.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Clinical psychologists can write prescriptions for antidepressant medications in every state after earning a doctorate.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Medical graduates must pass national licensing exams and complete supervised residency training before practicing independently.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Graduating from an accredited four-year medical school automatically grants a doctor a license to treat patients independently.

extra_socratic_questions: What training difference separates an osteopathic physician from an allopathic doctor during medical school?
Under what state licensing condition can a nurse practitioner prescribe medication without physician oversight?
Why is it dangerous to consult an optometrist instead of an ophthalmologist for detached retina surgery?
Which clinical doctoral degree focuses on psychotherapy and psychological testing rather than lab research?

extra_misconceptions.fact: Physician assistants hold master's degrees and are licensed clinicians who examine patients, order tests, and prescribe drugs.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Physician assistants are medical office helpers who only take vital signs and schedule patient appointments.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Paramedics complete over a thousand hours of advanced training to give intravenous drugs and intubate patients in the field.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Emergency medical technicians and paramedics have the same training and can administer identical cardiac medications.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Certified registered nurse anesthetists independently manage airway care and titrate anesthesia medications during surgery.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Certified nurse anesthetists only monitor asleep patients and must wait for a surgeon to adjust anesthesia doses.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Certified nursing assistants handle basic daily care and vital signs, while licensed practical nurses provide direct nursing care.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Licensed practical nurses and certified nursing assistants share the same legal authority to administer intravenous medications.

extra_socratic_questions: What clinical authority allows a physician assistant to diagnose illnesses while working on a medical team?
Which airway intervention can a paramedic perform in an ambulance that a basic EMT is not licensed to do?
Why must a pharmacist verify renal lab values before dispensing high-risk antibiotics to a hospital patient?
What scope of practice separates a registered nurse from a licensed practical nurse during patient triage?

extra_misconceptions.fact: Occupational therapists train patients of all ages to perform daily living skills like dressing, bathing, and eating safely.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Occupational therapists only help injured adults find new jobs or return to their workplace offices.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Registered dietitians must complete accredited clinical internships and pass a national board exam to provide nutrition therapy.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Any self-taught fitness coach can legally call themselves a registered dietitian and prescribe hospital medical nutrition.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Speech-language pathologists also evaluate and rehabilitate life-threatening swallowing disorders in post-stroke and trauma patients.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Speech-language pathologists only teach children how to pronounce consonant sounds and overcome stuttering.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Prosthetists examine patients and design custom sockets, while technicians fabricate and assemble the devices from specifications.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Prosthetists and medical appliance technicians perform the exact same clinical patient evaluations before building a limb.

extra_socratic_questions: What functional goal distinguishes occupational therapy from physical therapy after a patient suffers a stroke?
Which diagnostic swallow study allows a speech-language pathologist to detect silent aspiration of liquids?
Where should an orthotist place pressure-relief padding when casting a lower-limb socket for an amputee?
What blood gas measurement confirms that a respiratory therapist needs to adjust a patient's ventilator settings?

extra_misconceptions.fact: Radiology technologists position patients and capture scans, while radiologists are physicians who interpret the medical images.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Radiology technologists and radiologists are the same profession and both write official diagnostic medical reports.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Cross-contamination of chemical tube additives between needles and stoppers falsifies blood clotting and potassium lab results.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Drawing blood tubes in any random sequence produces accurate lab results as long as each tube fills completely.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Diagnostic ultrasound uses high-frequency sound waves rather than ionizing radiation to create real-time images of soft tissues.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Ultrasound sonographers expose pregnant patients to low doses of ionizing radiation during routine prenatal scans.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Histotechnologists slice and stain solid tissue biopsies, whereas cytopathologists are physicians who diagnose disease at the cell level.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Histotechnologists and cytopathologists perform identical lab work when examining patient fluid and tissue samples.

extra_socratic_questions: Why must a phlebotomist follow a strict order of draw when filling multiple vacuum blood collection tubes?
What physical energy wave does a diagnostic medical sonographer use to image fetal heart valves without radiation?
Which tissue preparation step must a histotechnologist complete before a pathologist can view a biopsy slide?
What shielding protocol protects a radiology technologist from scatter radiation during portable chest X-rays?

extra_misconceptions.fact: Most health care licenses require documented continuing education hours and periodic recertification exams to stay active.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Once a clinician passes their initial national board exam, their license remains valid for life without further testing.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Workplace visitors must obtain explicit patient consent and sign confidentiality agreements before observing any clinical care.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Student observers visiting a clinic are allowed to read any patient chart on the computer screen without permission.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Clinicians often spend several hours each day updating electronic health records and justifying treatments for insurance approval.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Health care professionals spend their entire shift treating patients and rarely spend time on documentation or billing codes.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Licensing boards only accept accredited courses, peer-reviewed workshops, and verified clinical seminars for renewal credit.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Continuing education credits can be earned by reading any popular health magazine or watching online medical dramas.

extra_socratic_questions: What infection-control steps must a Scout follow before entering a clinical workspace for job shadowing?
Why do state licensing boards require health care professionals to log continuing education credits every cycle?
Which workplace scheduling factor contributes most to clinician burnout during hospital night and weekend shifts?
What boundary must an observing Scout maintain if a patient asks a medical question during a clinic visit?

extra_misconceptions.fact: Medical schools use modernized oaths like the Declaration of Geneva or Lasagna's version, and taking an oath is an ethical tradition.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Every graduating physician in the United States is legally required to swear the original ancient Greek Hippocratic Oath.

extra_misconceptions.fact: That Latin maxim comes from a separate work by Hippocrates called Of the Epidemics rather than the formal oath text itself.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: The exact phrase 'first, do no harm' comes directly from the original text of the ancient Hippocratic Oath.

extra_misconceptions.fact: The oath is a moral pledge rather than a statute, though unethical actions may violate state medical practice laws and licensing rules.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Violating a line of the Hippocratic Oath automatically results in criminal arrest by federal law enforcement officers.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Modern medical ethics prioritizes patient autonomy, requiring informed consent before any test or procedure is performed.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: A physician's ethical duty to preserve life allows them to force medical treatment onto an informed, competent adult.

extra_socratic_questions: What ethical principle guides a physician when a surgery carries both a high benefit and a risk of harm?
Under what clinical condition must a doctor respect a competent adult patient's refusal of life-saving care?
Why have modern medical schools updated the ancient Hippocratic Oath into versions like the Declaration of Geneva?
Which duty in the Physician's Oath obligates doctors to share medical knowledge with the next generation?

extra_misconceptions.fact: HIPAA rules apply only to covered entities like health care providers, insurance plans, and clearinghouses, not private citizens.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: HIPAA prohibits anyone in the general public, including friends or teachers, from ever asking about a person's vaccination status.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Under the HIPAA minimum necessary rule, staff may only access charts for patients they are actively treating or supporting.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Any hospital nurse can legally open the electronic medical record of a famous celebrity patient just to check their status.

extra_misconceptions.fact: State and federal laws mandate that clinicians report specific infectious diseases, violent injuries, and abuse to authorities.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Patient confidentiality is absolute and prevents doctors from reporting gunshot wounds or suspected child abuse to police.

extra_misconceptions.fact: HIPAA safe harbor de-identification requires removing eighteen specific identifiers, including dates, zip codes, and account numbers.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Deleting a patient's name from a medical file is enough to make the record completely anonymous under federal privacy rules.

extra_socratic_questions: What happens to patient trust when a teenager fears a doctor will share sensitive health details with outsiders?
Under what public safety condition does federal law require a clinician to report patient information without consent?
Why is it dangerous to discuss a hospitalized neighbor's diagnosis in a public hospital elevator or cafeteria?
Which identifiers must be stripped from a medical chart before researchers can use the data as de-identified?

extra_misconceptions.fact: New treatments must pass years of multi-phase human clinical trials and FDA safety reviews before reaching routine patient care.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: A medical discovery that cures a disease in laboratory mice can be prescribed to human patients at hospitals the next month.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Surgical robots cannot make independent movements and only translate the precise hand controls of a trained surgeon at a console.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Robotic surgical systems operate autonomously in the operating room while the human surgeon watches from another room.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Messenger RNA never enters the cell nucleus where DNA is kept and breaks down quickly after teaching the immune system to respond.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Messenger RNA vaccines permanently alter a patient's nuclear DNA inside the chromosomes of their healthy body cells.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Clinical AI tools act as decision-support aids that highlight suspicious findings for a licensed physician to verify and sign.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Artificial intelligence diagnostic software is approved to replace human pathologists and radiologists in US hospitals today.

extra_socratic_questions: What clinical trial phase tests whether a new therapy is safer and more effective than the current standard of care?
Which home biometric measurement allows a cardiology team to detect fluid retention in a remote heart failure patient?
Under what condition does an artificial intelligence radiology tool create risk if a doctor accepts its output blindly?
What genetic editing mechanism allows CRISPR therapies to correct single-gene blood disorders like sickle cell disease?

extra_misconceptions.fact: Scouts must secure approval from both a parent or guardian and the merit badge counselor before starting volunteer service.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Volunteering at a local health fair counts toward Requirement 9 even if you ask your counselor for approval afterward.

extra_misconceptions.fact: All healthcare event volunteers must protect participant privacy and never share names or screening results in counselor reports.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Unpaid youth volunteers at a community blood pressure screening are exempt from patient privacy and HIPAA confidentiality rules.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Volunteers handle check-in, hospitality, and logistics, while only trained clinicians interpret vitals or offer medical guidance.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Youth volunteers at a blood drive or health fair may interpret blood pressure readings and give medical advice to visitors.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Canteen volunteers watch donors for pallor, sweating, or dizziness and immediately alert clinical staff if fainting signs appear.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Post-donation refreshment monitors at a blood drive only hand out snacks and have no role in donor safety observation.

extra_socratic_questions: Which approvals and site orientation steps are required before a Scout begins volunteering at a community health event?
Where does the boundary lie between a youth volunteer's logistical duties and a licensed clinician's medical tasks?
What details belong in your counselor report versus private patient health information that must never be recorded?
Why is it dangerous to let a blood donor leave the refreshment observation area before their recovery timer expires?
